Options · 2026-11-07, butt hook, five pairs and roundover 2026-11-09 · Bambu X2D, 0.6 nozzle

Rafter Rod Holder

A printed replacement for the two notched 1x4 combs on your garage joists. Your rods stay put until you pull a neighbour, then any bump drops one. Everything below is drawn to scale from one parameter file; the grams and times are from real slices (PETG, 2 walls, 15% infill, 0.30 mm layers). Two hooks now: one for the tip end of the rod, one with a 2 in opening for the grip.

Decided 2026-11-07 · second hook, five pairs and the roundover 2026-11-09

Deep hook, as individual printed hooks screwed to a 1x4, with a slot that leans away from the wood and no top bar; two versions, one for the tip end and one with a 2 in opening for the grip; five pairs on one plate; a very slight roundover on the front edges, the back and the bottom flat. Brian's words: "use the deep hook design ... make individual deep hooks, that can be screwed into a 1x4 piece of wood", then "make the bottom resting part of the hook have a slot that is angled to help keep the rod there better", "remove the top most part of the device that is not over the wood", "the slot should angle away from the wood", "5 holders should fit in the 20 in. There should be no space between each hook as it sits on the wood", "print these vertically so there can be much more in a single print", and on 2026-11-09: "There should be 2 versions of the holder. One that we already have is for the rod tip end. The rod butt end should be able to accommodate a 2 in rod handle. The rods I have are 1 7/8 in or so. Make it a 2 in opening ... make both versions in the same file, vertical", "the holders will stack on top of each other, make sure there is 2 in of room to get the butt in", "there should only be 5 pairs", "all edges should have a very slight roundover", "do not add a round over to the back of the part. Use this flat surface to print the part vertically." PETG. Both hooks are built and checked below; the concept round is kept underneath for the record.

Built · two rod hooks, one file, one plate

Two printed hooks share one tab: 4 in tall, 3/8 thick, two #8 x 1 in screws 1 in from the board edge, five butted end to end filling a board's 20 in hang so the rods land every 4 in. Every edge on the front has a 1/32 in roundover; the back face that sits on the wood and the bottom edge the print stands on are flat and square. The tip hook (4 x 4 in) carries a 7/8 in slot leaning 35 degrees for the blank; the butt hook (4.5 x 4 in) a 2 in slot leaning 10 degrees for the grip (your handles are about 1-7/8). A rod lies across a tip board at one joist and a butt board at another, as on your combs. Both are open Js: the rod drops in at the top, slides down the ramp away from the board and rests at the bottom; to leave it has to come back up toward the board, over the lip tip and under the hook above. The lip top slopes up to its tip, so a rod set on it rolls in. Nothing touches the wood; the boards hang from the joists exactly as your combs do.

Why the butt hook looks the way it does

  • The 4 in pitch is the budget. A 1-7/8 grip must pass between the lip tip and the hook stacked 4 in above (the top hook has the joist there), so the tip sits at 1-3/4: a 2.25 in gap to get the butt in, against the 2 in you asked for (the script fails under 2); 3/8 to spare on your grips, 1/4 on a 2 in one.
  • Under that: a 5/16 floor, the 2 in rounded bottom, and a 10 degree lean, the most that still leaves the lip a straight inner face. The tip hook's 35 degrees with a 2 in slot would want a 7 in hook.
  • So the hold here is all lift: 1.41 in up the near-vertical slot before the grip can come over the lip. Same mechanism, same bump tolerance, no hood.
  • The opening is 2 in as asked: 1/16 clear of each wall on a 1-7/8 grip. Measure your fattest grip (and any reel seat the hook lands on) before printing the five; the slot width is one constant.

Checks baked into the script, both hooks

  • Hold. Pose-space check with the hooks above and below and the board in the way: the rod centre must rise 1.57 in (1/4 blank), 1.57 in (3/8) and 1.57 in (5/8) in the tip hook, 1.41 in (1-1/2 grip), 1.41 in (1-3/4) and 1.41 in (1-7/8) in the butt hook, before any path to the outside opens; the plain deep hook gave 1.00. A bump moves a rod millimetres, and a hop lands it back on the ramp, which slides it home.
  • Way in. Every size reaches its slot from outside past the hook butted above, so nothing is trapped either way; the gap over the lip tip is 1.75 in on the tip hook and 2.25 on the butt hook.
  • Clearances. Seated rods and grips touch neither the hook's walls beyond their resting contact nor the board; the hooks sit flat on the board face.
  • Printable standing. Both print on the 4 in bottom edge, face vertical, all ten on one plate. That bottom edge and the back face are flat and square (no roundover there), so the print stands on a full flat strip; the 1/32 in roundover runs along the front face's edges and the countersink rims. Steepest overhang, read layer by layer the way the slicer sees it: 35 degrees from vertical on the tip hook (the slot lean), 10 on the butt hook, under the 45 degree limit; the screw holes print sideways (5 mm bridges, fine). Thinnest wall 1/8 in (3.2 mm) against the 1.24 mm minimum; lips 0.58 and 0.55 in at their thinnest. Layers run across the hook, so a sideways yank on a lip loads the layer bond; at rod loads that is a 3x margin.
  • Exported STLs are watertight, one solid each, 63.8 and 58.2 cm3.

How we got here · the concept round, 2026-11-07

Why they fall out

A half-round cut into a vertical edge has its lowest point at the edge. The rod rolls down the arc and rests at the mouth with nothing in front of it. A hook pocket puts the floor inside the plate behind a lip, so a rod has to rise over the lip before it can leave.

The comb in place

Same idea as your boards: a plate screwed to the side face of the joist, hanging straight down, rods lying across two of them. It is 2-1/2 in wide and 1/2 in thick, hangs 17 in below the joist (yours hang 20), and holds four rods 4 in apart. The mouths face the same way your notches do.

Decision 1 · Pocket shape

A · Hook pocket

5/8 inlift to leave
  • Level mouth: slide the rod in, let it drop.
  • Any blank from 1/4 to 5/8 in sits in the 7/8 in pocket.
  • No moving parts, nothing to relax over the years.
Picked

B · Deep hook

1 inlift to leave
  • Mouth higher than the lip: the rod rolls into the pocket by itself.
  • Harder to lift out overhead; each pocket is 3/8 in taller, so the comb grows or the pitch does.
  • Then reworked on Brian's ask into the open J with the angled slot (built section above).
Fit per rod size

C · Snap clip

Gripsevery direction
  • PETG spring fingers close over the blank.
  • Fits 5/16 to 7/16 in blanks only; thinner rods rattle, thicker ones will not go in.
  • Springs relax in a hot garage.

Decision 2 · What gets printed

Picked: a blend Individual printed hooks on a plain 1x4: B's wood backbone and screw-on pieces, without the old notches, and A's pocket in every hook.

A · Printed comb, three pieces

154 gper comb, 3 h 08 min
pair: 308 g, 6 h 16 min
  • Mount 48 g, module 56 g, end module 51 g; every piece lies flat on the bed.
  • Half-laps with two M4 bolts; the mount takes three #8 x 1-1/2 wood screws.
  • Two rods: mount plus end module, 99 g, hang 9 in. Six rods would hang 25 in, so a second pair instead.
Cheapest fix

B · Caps on your wood combs

20 gper cap, 28 min
your 7 notches: 137 g, 3 h 16 min
  • One cap per notch, 2-3/4 x 3-1/4 x 3/8 in, two #8 screws into the board, mouth 1 in proud of the edge.
  • The boards, their 20 in hang and the 5 in spacing stay as they are.
  • Same hook pocket; the rod ends up inside the old notch.

Decision 3 · Material

MaterialOne combPair7 capsVerdict
PETG Recommended154 g, 3 h 08 min308 g137 gHolds its shape in a hot garage under a load that never comes off. Same spool as the NACS and skateboard holders.
PLA151 g, 3 h 08 min301 g134 gSaves nothing worth having and creeps when a summer ceiling goes past 45 C with rods hanging on it.
ASA130 g, 3 h 08 min260 g116 gOnly if that ceiling bakes above 70 C. Needs the chamber in heat mode.

PLA and ASA grams are the PETG slice scaled by density; times carry over. Rods are light: four with reels are under 3 lb per comb.

What I assumed, and what the side view asks

  • Joists 2x8 at 16 in on centre (the 7 in of board above the joist bottom matched a 2x8).
  • Rods per comb 4, like your longer board. Modules add two at a time.
  • Pitch 4 in, first rod 4 in below the joist. If reels stay on and line up, go 5 in or stagger the handles.
  • Blank at the comb 1/4 to 5/8 in; pocket 7/8 in, mouth 1-1/4 in tall.
  • Hang 17 in clears the open door the way your 20 in does.
  • Mouth faces the same way as your notches; say so if it should flip.
  • Screws three #8 x 1-1/2 into the joist, solid pads around every hole in the 3MF.
  • Comb spacing unknown; it only matters for the rods, not the print.

Your picks

Pocket and build are decided (above). The buttons stay for the open items: material, rods per comb, reels.
